assembled_remainder.all_j_ge_2: o(B(log B)^(1/3)) by the positive j=2 zero-channel majorant
assembled_remainder.j1_nonzero_harmonics_core: o(B(log B)^(1/3)) by finite Vaaler truncation plus polylog-uniform Hecke cancellation
assembled_remainder.minimal_scale: O(B)=o(B(log B)^(1/3)) for the largest j=1 zero boundary
assembled_remainder.result: Every term other than the j=1 zero bulk is o(B(log B)^(1/3)).

final_stage13_7i_conclusion.pure_G_ac_minus_bc: Delta_G(B) ~ K0 B(log B)^(1/3), with K0>0 as evaluated in curved_wedge_asymptotic_report.json.
final_stage13_7i_conclusion.reason_ratio_not_claimed: 7i proves the secondary ac-bc gap for the pure-G observable; a separate asymptotic for the individual G-neutral category masses is required before turning this into an ac/bc ratio limit statement.

finite_fourier_majorant.constant_term_error: O(1/L) times the positive j=1 zero-channel mass
finite_fourier_majorant.degree: L=(log B)^K with any fixed K>1/12; K=4 is a convenient choice
finite_fourier_majorant.pointwise_feature: The interval indicator is bracketed pointwise, so no uniform Fejer convergence at moving jump locations is assumed.
finite_fourier_majorant.tool: standard Selberg/Vaaler trigonometric majorant/minorant for interval indicators
finite_fourier_majorant.truncation_error: Since the positive j=1 mass on the retained wedge is O(B(log B)^(1/3)), the majorant/minorant excess is O(B(log B)^(1/3)/L)=o(B(log B)^(1/3)).

metadata.scope: uniform nonzero-harmonic closure and all-j normalization tail

normalization_remainder.boundary_and_wings: The separated minimal-scale and small-height/coordinate regions are at most O(B(log B)^(1/4)), hence o(B(log B)^(1/3)).
normalization_remainder.consequence: All j>=2 zero and nonzero angular content is dominated at once by 3/2 times the positive j=2 zero channel; no uniform summation over j or ell is needed.
normalization_remainder.identity: After extracting j=1, the exact denominator remainder is 1/(G-1)-1/G = 1/(G(G-1)).
normalization_remainder.j2_bulk: Stage13-7h exponent: B(log B)^(-5/9) on the core
normalization_remainder.pointwise_majorant: If N is the signed primitive face-gap numerator and T_G is the positive primitive face-count numerator, |N|<=T_G.  Since G>=3, |N|/(G(G-1)) <= (3/2) T_G/G^2.

outer_coefficient_bv.consequence: Boxwise partial summation costs a constant independent of ell; the growth of the oscillation count is cancelled by the 1/ell Fourier amplitude.

uniform_hecke_input.curved_core: After the 7h rectangle and bounded-variation transfer, each retained harmonic is O_{A,K}(B(log B)^(-A)); summing at most L=log(B)^K modes remains lower order after choosing A>K+10.
uniform_hecke_input.polylog_uniformity: For ell<=log(B)^K, conductor dependence is only polylogarithmic.  Together with uniform local majorants from 7h and polynomial vertical growth, the z=0 scale contour/finite-order Selberg-Delange argument gives, for every fixed A,K, a bound O_{A,K}(X(log X)^(-A)) uniformly in this ell range.
uniform_hecke_input.reference_boundary: For example Merikoski, On Gaussian primes in sparse sets, Sec. 2.7, Lemma 2.13 (classical Landau-Page zero-free region, citing Iwaniec-Kowalski Ch.5).
uniform_hecke_input.zero_free_region: Use the standard Hecke zero-free region with analytic-conductor dependence log((2+|t|)(2+|k|)); the possible exceptional real zero occurs only for k=0, so it is absent for xi_{8ell}, ell>=1.
